passage:
Dear Mummy,

I'm writing this because I get tongue-tied when we talk. I know you check my phone each night, and that you started after the group chat mess. I understand you were scared. But it makes me feel watched, and I've started deleting messages just to feel private, which I don't like doing.

Can you tell me exactly what you're worried about? I'll show you my chats myself on Sunday evenings for now, and I promise I won't make secret accounts. Could we look at it again in a couple of months, and if I've been open, you check less?

Thanks for reading this. 🙂

Sarika

P.S. I'll be in the kitchen. Irawati Auntie next door says hi.

qa.q: On which evenings does Sarika offer to show the chats?
qa.a: Sarika offers to show them on Sunday evenings.

qa.q: What is Sarika feeling about the nightly phone checks, and how does it show?
qa.a: Sarika feels watched and uneasy, and it shows in how Sarika has started deleting messages just to feel private.

qa.q: What is Sarika doing that could help build trust with Mummy?
qa.a: Sarika asks for a clear reason, promises no secret accounts, shares the chats openly and suggests a review in a couple of months, so constant checking becomes less needed.

qa.q: How might Sarika's mother feel when she reads the letter?
qa.a: Probably relieved that Sarika is talking openly, and maybe a little sad to hear the checking hurt, while still worried about what caused it.

grounding: Shows a teen whose phone is monitored writing to ask for a clear reason and a path to more trust, sharing openly and promising no secret accounts.

passage:
I'm Tanvir. When I was sixteen, Abbu put a monitoring app on my phone. Every search, every chat, he could see. I felt like I was living under a CCTV camera. I deleted messages even when they were harmless, just to feel I had some privacy.
My friend Varun said, "Easy. Make a second account. They'll never know." For one night I thought about it. But I knew that if Abbu found it, I would never get his trust back.
So I asked him straight: "Why? What happened?" He told me about a boy in a colleague's family who got caught in an online scam. He was scared. I said, "Then tell me what I need to show you for this app to go." We agreed on three months, and I would tell him about new contacts myself. After three months, he deleted it in front of me.

qa.a: Making a second account the parents would never know about.

qa.q: How did Tanvir feel with the monitoring app?
qa.a: Uneasy and trapped, as if living under a CCTV camera, deleting even harmless messages to feel some privacy.

qa.q: Why was asking Abbu directly better than a secret account?
qa.a: It uncovered his real fear and created a clear path to trust, while a secret account could have destroyed trust if found.
Fear, after a boy in a colleague's family got caught in an online scam.

grounding: A teenager whose phone is monitored feels watched, rejects a secret account and asks for a reason and a path to more trust.

passage:
Counsellor's note, Tuesday
Madhav was referred after his mother, Mrs. Ganga Rao, found a second social media account he had hidden from her. She has checked his phone every night since. Madhav said, "She reads everything. I made the other account just to breathe." His mother replied, "And now I can't believe anything you show me."
Both were hurt. I asked Madhav what he needed: a reason, and a way to earn back privacy. I asked his mother what she needed: to know who he talks to, and no more hidden accounts.
They agreed that he would delete the second account in front of her and tell her about new online contacts himself, and she would move from nightly checks to a weekly talk. We will review in six weeks. Madhav left saying, "I didn't know she was that scared."

qa.q: How often will Mrs. Rao talk with Madhav instead of checking nightly?
Why did Madhav make the second account?
qa.a: He felt watched and suffocated by the nightly checks and wanted space to breathe.

qa.q: How did the secret account backfire, and what plan rebuilt trust?
qa.a: It made his mother doubt everything; the plan was to delete it in front of her, share new contacts himself and move to weekly talks.

qa.q: How does Mrs. Rao see the hidden account?
qa.a: As broken trust; she can no longer believe what he shows her, and her checking comes from fear.

grounding: A counsellor's note shows a monitored teen whose secret account damaged trust, and how a clear reason and a path to trust replace constant checking.
